ref_extractions.title: Human emotion recognition from EEG-based brain–computer interface using machine learning: a comprehensive review
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is a comprehensive review paper on EEG-based emotion recognition methods, not an original study using a specific dataset. It discusses datasets generally but does not mention or use openneuro_ds006554.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Review paper; no specific dataset identified

ref_extractions.title: Motor resonance during linguistic processing as shown by EEG in a naturalistic VR environment
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This study uses EEG with a Go/No-Go task in a VR environment examining motor resonance during action verb processing. It does not use openneuro_ds006554 and has a different paradigm focused on language-motor interaction rather than social observation.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different paradigm: motor resonance with language in VR

ref_extractions.title: The Simulation of Smiles (SIMS) model: Embodied simulation and the meaning of facial expression
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is a theoretical review article about embodied simulation in facial expression recognition. It does not present experimental EEG data or use any specific dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Theoretical review; no experimental EEG data

ref_extractions.title: Shared computational principles for language processing in humans and deep language models
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This study uses ECoG (electrocorticography) recorded while participants listened to podcasts, examining language prediction mechanisms. It does not use openneuro_ds006554 and uses ECoG rather than scalp EEG.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different modality: ECoG; different paradigm: language prediction

ref_extractions.title: Mental workload and neural efficiency quantified in the prefrontal cortex using fNIRS
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This study uses fNIRS (functional near-infrared spectroscopy) to measure prefrontal activation during flight simulation and cognitive tasks. It does not use EEG and does not reference openneuro_ds006554.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different modality: fNIRS; different paradigm: mental workload

ref_extractions.title: Neurocomputational mechanisms of social presence effects on instrumental learning
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This study records EEG during a probabilistic learning task with or without social observation (confederate present). While it involves social observation and EEG, this is a separate experiment not using openneuro_ds006554. The paradigm differs significantly (instrumental learning vs social observation of stimuli).
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Related topic but different experiment; does not use openneuro_ds006554

ref_extractions.title: Precursors to morality in development as a complex interplay between neural, socioenvironmental, and behavioral facets
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This study examines infant neural responses to prosocial/antisocial behaviors using EEG and eye-tracking. It does not use openneuro_ds006554 and focuses on developmental morality rather than social observation in adults.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different population: infants; different paradigm: moral cognition

ref_extractions.title: Social status determines how we monitor and evaluate our performance
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This study uses EEG during a time estimation task while manipulating social hierarchy and status. It does not use openneuro_ds006554 and has a different experimental paradigm focused on social evaluation.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different paradigm: social status evaluation with time estimation

ref_extractions.title: Dissociable processing of emotional and neutral body movements revealed by μ-alpha and beta rhythms
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This study examines mu-suppression and beta rhythms while viewing emotional vs neutral body movements (point-light displays). It does not use openneuro_ds006554 and focuses on embodied emotion simulation.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different paradigm: body movement perception; mu suppression

ref_extractions.title: REBUS and the Anarchic Brain: Toward a Unified Model of the Brain Action of Psychedelics
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is a theoretical review paper proposing a model of psychedelic brain action. It does not present experimental EEG data using openneuro_ds006554 or any specific dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Theoretical model paper; no experimental data

ref_extractions.title: Role of the occipito-temporal theta rhythm in hand visual identification
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This study examines theta-band activity during hand visual identification using a match-to-sample task. It does not use openneuro_ds006554 and focuses on body-part processing rather than social observation.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different paradigm: hand identification; theta oscillations

ref_extractions.title: Machine Learning for Healthcare Wearable Devices: The Big Picture
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is a review article about machine learning applications for healthcare wearable devices. It does not use openneuro_ds006554 or any specific EEG dataset, and is not focused on social observation.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Review paper on wearable ML; no specific dataset

ref_extractions.title: Early Anticipation Lies behind the Speed of Response in Conversation
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This study examines EEG correlates of turn-end anticipation in conversation using a key-press task. It does not use openneuro_ds006554 and focuses on conversational timing rather than social observation of stimuli.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different paradigm: conversation turn-taking

ref_extractions.title: Questions and controversies in the study of time-varying functional connectivity in resting fMRI
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is a review paper about resting fMRI functional connectivity methods. It does not use EEG, does not use openneuro_ds006554, and focuses on fMRI methodology rather than social observation.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different modality: fMRI; review paper

ref_extractions.title: EEG complexity as a biomarker for autism spectrum disorder risk
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This study uses resting-state EEG complexity (mMSE) to classify infants at high vs low risk for autism. It does not use openneuro_ds006554 and has a different population (infants) and paradigm (resting-state ASD screening).
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different population: infants; different paradigm: ASD risk classification

ref_extractions.title: Linking Out-of-Body Experience and Self Processing to Mental Own-Body Imagery at the Temporoparietal Junction
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This study examines EEG correlates of mental body transformation tasks related to out-of-body experiences. It does not use openneuro_ds006554 and focuses on self-processing rather than social observation.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different paradigm: self/body imagery; TMS-EEG

ref_extractions.title: The Representation of Biological Classes in the Human Brain
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This study uses fMRI to examine category representation of animal species in visual cortex. It does not use openneuro_ds006554 and uses fMRI rather than EEG, with a different focus on category representation.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different modality: fMRI; different paradigm: category representation

ref_extractions.title: How robust is the language architecture? The case of mood
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This study examines mood effects on language comprehension using reading tasks and ERPs. It does not use openneuro_ds006554 and focuses on mood-language interactions rather than social observation.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different paradigm: mood effects on reading

ref_extractions.title: Working Memory From the Psychological and Neurosciences Perspectives: A Review
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is a review article about working memory models and neural correlates. It does not present experimental data using openneuro_ds006554 and is not focused on social observation.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Review paper; no experimental dataset

ref_extractions.title: Emotion Classification from Electroencephalographic Signals Using Machine Learning
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This study uses the SEED-V dataset to classify emotions from EEG signals using neural networks. It does not use openneuro_ds006554 and uses a different dataset (SEED-V) specifically designed for emotion recognition.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Uses SEED-V dataset, not openneuro_ds006554

ref_extractions.title: Functional connectivity in infants' visual cortex and its links to motion processing and autism
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This study examines EEG functional connectivity in 5-month-old infants watching social vs non-social videos. It does not use openneuro_ds006554 and has a different population (infants) focused on autism markers.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different population: infants; different focus: autism connectivity

feasibility_reason: The dataset has a clear, well-documented event structure with 30 identifiable social stimulus condition labels across 47 subjects, enabling epoch-based classification tasks. Although all reference papers are irrelevant or uncertain, this is a well-documented public OpenNeuro dataset with a clear social observation paradigm, satisfying the exception criterion for feasibility.
